job.location: Various School Sites in Newport Beach and Costa Mesa, CA

items.item_text: 01. Information I provide to the following supplemental questions will be reviewed as part of the application process. Questions that are not fully and completely answered will be considered grounds for disqualification from the examination process. Stating "see resume" in lieu of a complete response to these questions is not acceptable. Select "Yes" to indicate that you have read and understand these instructions. Options: Yes
02. Do you have a high school diploma or equivalent? Options: Yes, I have a high school diploma or GED | No, I do not have a high school diploma nor GED

03. Do you have a valid First Aid/CPR Certification? Options: Yes | No, but I am willing to obtain a valid certification within the first six months of employment | No, and I am not willing to obtain one
04. Do you have a valid California Driver's License (or an out-of-state license and are willing to obtain a California Driver's License upon offer of employment)? Options: Yes | No

05. These positions can work at various school site settings. Please select all the types of school site preferences you would be willing to work at: Options: College Park Elementary - 6 hours/day | Rea Elementary - 6 hours/day | Victoria Elementary - 8 hours/day

06. How many years of verifiable job related experience do you have working with children in an educational, recreational or child care setting? Options: None | Less than 1 year | 1-2 years | 2-3 years | 3 years or more

07. How many years of verifiable job related work experience do you have observing and controlling the behavior of students in or outside of the classroom? Options: None | Less than 1 year | 1-2 years | 2-3 years | 3 years or more
08. How many years of experience do you have monitoring and evaluating student progress? Options: None | Less than 1 year | 1-2 years | 2-3 years | 3 years or more
09. How many years of verifiable job related work experience do you have in a lead or supervisory capacity? Options: None | Less than 1 year | 1-2 years | 2-3 years | 3 years or more

10. Do you have the ability to perform oral and written translations to/from English and Spanish? NOTE: Some vacancies requires this ability. Options: Yes, I am fluent in English and Spanish | No, I do not speak Spanish

11. How many years of verifiable job related work experience do you have performing oral and written translations to/from English and Spanish? NOTE: Some vacancies requires this ability. Options: None | Less than 1 year | 1-2 years | 2-3 years | 4 years or more
12. Have you previously taken the No Child Left Behind exam? Options: Yes | No

13. If you answered YES to the question above, please select the school district where you took the NCLB exam. Options: Fountain Valley School District | Huntington Beach City School District | Huntington Beach Union High School District | Newport-Mesa Unified School District | Ocean View School District | None of the above
14. Are you available to work Monday through Friday 12:30 p.m. to 6:30 p.m. during the school year? Options: Yes | No
15. Do you have experience with basic instructional methods and techniques? Options: Yes | No
16. Are you familiar with standard office equipment, including the ability to keep records on a computer? Options: Yes | No

17. The questions below are designed to indicate whether you are willing to perform the duty listed. Check YES if you are willing to perform this duty or NO if you are not. Please keep in mind that all of the duties listed are REQUIRED of the position. If you are not willing to do any one of the duties listed, you will not be considered in the recruitment process. Select "Yes" to indicate that you have read and understand these instructions. Options: Yes
18. Monitor and coordinate extended day programs at assigned sites. Options: Yes | No
19. Train and provide work direction to assigned staff. Options: Yes | No
20. Observe and monitor students inside and outside the classroom. Options: Yes | No
21. Perform minor first aid to students with illnesses or injuries. Options: Yes | No
22. Maintain confidentiality of student records and related materials. Options: Yes | No
23. Participate in meetings and in-service training program. Options: Yes | No
24. Please describe your experience working with students in an educational setting.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES: Oversee and provide guidance to assigned staff in the coordination of Extended Day Program operations at multiple assigned sites; serve as liaison between extended day site staff, the Director and/or Coordinator and Site Principal; prepare, organize and maintain site instructional materials to support staff and promote students learning. Monitor and coordinate extended day programs at assigned sites; assure compliance with Program policies and procedures; implement approved academic and enrichment activities for students. Train and provide work direction to assigned personnel; provide input and assistance in the selection and evaluation of new staff; prepare work schedules for assigned staff; adjust staff schedules as needed; review assigned staff time cards and report tardiness to program director. Communicate with parents, administrators, principals, personnel and outside agencies to exchange information and resolve issues or concerns. Perform instructional assistant duties in the absence of assigned staff. Assist in the collection, preparation and maintenance of screening and assessment data. Prepare and maintain a variety of records, logs, reports, notes and files; compose email correspondence independently. Assist in managing budget at assigned site; inventory and order supplies for assigned sites; submit purchase orders and receipt reimbursements to administration. Monitor and manage extended day program attendance database; review attendance sheets for accuracy. Support and ensure timely pick up of all students at assigned sites and assist staff with resolving issues of students left after center closes. Monitor students in program activities and perform recess supervision guiding students into safe play activities. Assist students to develop communication skills and serve as an appropriate language model. Perform routine first aid and seek assistance for non-routine illnesses or injuries; assure the health and safety of students by following health and safety practices and procedures. Participate in staff meetings and attend in-services as required. Maintain classroom in a safe, sanitary and orderly condition. Operate a variety of audio-visual, office and instructional equipment. Drive a vehicle to conduct work and to travel to assigned school sites. OTHER DUTIES: Perform related duties as assigned. KNOWLEDGE AND ABILITIES: KNOWLEDGE OF: Child development strategies. District and site policies, procedures and regulations. After school program curriculum and lesson planning. Basic instructional methods and techniques. Classroom procedures and appropriate student conduct. Student supervision principles and practices. Student behavior management techniques Goals and objectives of assigned program. Basic record keeping and budgeting techniques. Basic math concepts and applications. Health and safety regulations. Operation of standard office equipment, including a computer and appropriate software. Correct English usage, grammar, spelling, punctuation and vocabulary. Interpersonal skills using tact, patience and courtesy. Nutrition needs for students. ABILITY TO: Read, interpret, apply and explain rules, regulations, policies and procedures applicable to child care. Assist with instruction and related activities in a classroom or assigned outdoor environment. Prepare a variety of instructional support materials. Reinforce instruction to individual or small groups of students. Compile data and prepare records. Maintain records and files. Understand and follow oral directions. Operate a variety of standard office equipment, including a computer and appropriate software. Perform clerical duties related to classroom activities. Monitor and evaluate student progress. Organize and disperse instructional materials. Lead, encourage and support assigned extended day program staff. Work independently. Establish and maintain cooperative and effective working relationships with others. Communicate effectively both orally and in writing. Monitor, observe and report student behavior and progress according to approved policies and procedures. Attend meetings and in-services as required. WORKING CONDITIONS: ENVIRONMENT: Office, classroom and playground settings. Drive a vehicle to conduct work at multiple assigned sites. PHYSICAL DEMANDS: Sitting or standing for extend periods of time. Driving to assigned sites. Bending at the waist, kneeling, crawling, or crouching to assist students. Hearing and speaking to exchange information. Seeing to monitor students. Dexterity of hands and fingers to operate standard classroom equipment. Ewing Consulting, Inc. January 2022
